claims.text: Adding 5–10 wt.% Ni before consolidation and annealing at approximately 1000°C for 1 hour will cause Ni to segregate to W–Cu interfaces.
The segregated Ni will form Ni-rich interfacial layers at W–Cu boundaries.
Ni segregation lowers the W–Cu interfacial energy.
Ni-rich interfacial layers serve as effective diffusion barriers.
The proposed diffusion-barrier effect suppresses diffusion-driven phase separation during thermal and irradiation exposure.
The proposed interfacial modification inhibits void nucleation and interfacial void formation during thermal and irradiation exposure.
Ni-treated composites will have improved interfacial bonding relative to untreated W–Cu composites.
Reduced interfacial void formation will produce higher thermal conductivity in Ni-treated composites than in untreated composites under elevated heat-transfer conditions.
Ni-treated composites will retain higher thermal conductivity than untreated composites under irradiation conditions relevant to W-based plasma-facing material and Cu-based cooling-component joints.
Untreated W–Cu composites typically undergo phase separation and interfacial void formation under severe thermal and irradiation conditions.
Phase separation and interfacial void formation diminish the thermal conductivity of untreated W–Cu composites over time.
